newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets end steady after quiet session.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets end steady after quiet session.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close

OVERNIGHT CASH 9.45 PCT (PREV 9.45) US 30-YR 6.69 (PREV 6.84)
* NZ bank bills end higher as futures sold, TWI falls
* Mid bonds lose early gains, 10-years hold in
* Apathetic market awaits catalyst for further action
New Zealand debt markets ended almost on their opening levels on Wednesday after a quiet session, particularly in the bonds.

Bonds began on a strong note, driven by a U.S. market rally on the back of market-friendly employment cost data, although the extent of the local rally was limited and New Zealand bonds underperformed the U.S.
Mid bonds relinquished some of their gains to end a couple of points higher in yield. The benchmark 10-year bond held in at 7.26 percent, down seven basis points from its close on Tuesday.
One dealer said he had got the impression many offshore investors thought the U.S. rally was well and truly overdone, which could explain New Zealand's underperformance.
"It shouldn't have gone that far. The (employment cost) number was good but it wasn't that flash," he said.
Dealers said volumes were light and traders seemed content to sit reasonably square in the absence of significant offshore flows.

"There has been little to nothing going on, just bits and pieces here and there...people aren't wanting to go out and aggressively buy it down here and there's nobody with real interest to sell it, so it's just sitting here with people waiting for a flow one way or the other to spur it on," a Wellington dealer said.

"They seem reasonably happy to hold here and not do much. They're long, they're happy, and it's going to take something for them to get out, maybe another spike down for whatever reason, before they maybe look at taking profit."

In the money market, 90-day bank bills continued to edge higher throughout the day after a failed attempt to follow the bonds lower. They ended at 8.97 percent, while the December and March 1997 futures contracts encountered good selling interest to finish down 10 points each at 91.50 and 92.15 respectively.
The currency's Trade-Weighted Index fell a further 20 basis points during the session, after opening 20 points lower. --------------------------(SPREADS)----------------------------
